Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually come with that many software limitations. Not only can most major PC applications run on this platform, but there are also plenty of useful Mac-exclusive applications.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games running on Mac have reached their best-ever performance...

Apple has an exclusive game porting toolkit that helps developers evaluate how their Windows games run on Mac, with the aim of encouraging and facilitating them to port their games to the Mac platform.

However, as Filipe Esposito of Macworld mentioned, this toolkit is also used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac—himself being one of them. He pointed out that the latest test version brings significant performance improvements, citing GTA V as an example.

After testing the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta for several days on a MacBook Pro with M4 Pro, he found that the performance boost fundamentally changed the experience of running demanding Windows games... On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using identical game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from around 106 fps on GPTK 3 to about 176 fps on GPTK 4 beta—an increase of approximately 66%. The game ran quite smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings at 2K resolution.

He acknowledged that not every game sees such dramatic improvements, but hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
